note: Structured state for known gaps/exclusions/risks — CONSUMED by tests/expected_fails_check.d (schema + kind + probe-target existence). Each entry has an id, area, reason, since, remove_when, and a `kind`: `permanent_exclusion` (not public API / platform), `known_gap` (a generator limitation with no failing target), or `risk` (a private-API dependency that MUST keep compiling — its `probe_targets` name the build targets that guard it, and the checker verifies those targets exist).

entries.reason: QUiLoader-only private Qt widgets (QFileDialog internals, QtGradient editors, qprintpropertieswidget) are not public API, so the differential oracle can't hold them.
entries.remove_when: never (these are not public Qt API)

entries.reason: An overridden virtual that returns a container/QList still dispatches non-virtually — the C++ method shim can't sret those, so it falls back to the direct-symbol guard. No known Qt override is affected.
A method with a move-only (deleted-copy) by-value param uses the direct pragma decl, or is dropped if inline — the shim/guard would copy the param.
entries.remove_when: the shim forwards value params by std::move

entries.reason: Linux/POSIX is Tier 1; Windows/MSVC-x64 is a documented roadmap (docs/windows-roadmap.md), not tested.
entries.remove_when: the windows-roadmap tiers are implemented and green

entries.reason: qmlRegisterType fills QQmlPrivate::RegisterType and calls QQmlPrivate::qmlregister — a private struct whose layout differs Qt5<->Qt6 (handled behind a QT_VERSION seam) and can shift between Qt minor versions.
entries.remove_when: Qt exposes a public API to register a runtime QMetaObject as a QML type, or the probe runs across a Qt-version matrix in CI

entries.reason: All D @QObject types registered via qmlRegisterType share one C++ typeId (QtdMocObject* on Qt6, QObjectStar on Qt5), differing only by runtime QMetaObject. On Qt6 this makes a TYPED cross-property assignment (`property Alpha a: Alpha{}`) fail QML's metatype assignability check. Instantiation and `property var` work on both; the qmltwo test proves N distinct types coexist.
entries.remove_when: each registered runtime type gets a DISTINCT QMetaType (a dynamic QMetaTypeInterface per type) instead of the shared carrier metatype

entries.reason: .qmltypes validation uses QQmlJSTypeDescriptionReader from Qt6QmlCompiler private API (the reader qmllint/qmltyperegistrar use). Qt6-only; can change across versions.
entries.remove_when: a public qmltypes parser ships, or the probe runs across a Qt-version matrix

entries.reason: The runtime moc (qtdmoc.cpp) builds QMetaObjects with QMetaObjectBuilder, a Qt private API. Long-standing dependency; every moc/qml/tr target compiles against it.
entries.remove_when: never expected (no public equivalent); revisit if Qt ships a public runtime-metaobject builder

entries.reason: The `-all-` (--objpaths/--dumpall) target is not built for 2 fixtures, and it is not a gap: a `Connections` element is desugared into connects and no object is built, while the engine holds one in `conn` — both fixtures say so in their own headers. Connect, CrossCall. Permanent for this protocol. Everything else this entry once listed is DONE (2026-08-03): ALIASES (qtmoc gained @PropertyAlias — a forwarding property backed by a getter and a `<name>_set`, for a scalar target and for an object one); DEFAULT-PROPERTY HOLDERS (a declared object property exists even when its type maps to no D wrapper, and a single-object default property is ASSIGNED, not only appended); LIST PROPERTIES (a meta-object QQmlListProperty whose elements the runtime owns — it needs the metatype AND the element type registered with QQmlMetaType, and the registration has to run from a function because --gc-sections removes a file-scope static nothing reads); and the `__class` label, now decided in the emitter. Measured: controls 23 of 23, quick 46 of 46, corpus 44 of 46.
entries.remove_when: never for the Connections pair — it is a deliberate structural difference.

entries.reason: The WEAK protocol's independent half (`--verify-props`) fails when the engine built a QML-declared member no label mentions. An item a VIEW creates has no static path, so `--labels` drops it by design, and a delegate that declares properties trips a guard that was never able to name those objects at all -- it is not the "both sides shrank" case the guard exists to catch. `labelsGap` in reggaefile.d exempts exactly the five delegate fixtures (QDelegateKidCtx, QDelegateRole, QDelegateRoleReq, QDelegateReqNoModel, QDelegateReqFill) from that half only; the diff of the values it DID record still runs, and the STRONG `-all-` target beside it compares those items properly and is green for all five.
entries.remove_when: `--labels` can name an object a view creates (it would need the index the view decides, which is what `--objpaths`/`--dumpall` already asks at run time)

entries.reason: The node that generates a fixture's D treats exit 3 (PARTIAL: members skipped and reported) as failure, deliberately, so no fixture can quietly go partial. Two fixtures cannot satisfy that because their REFUSAL is what they measure: QDelegateReqNoModel (a delegate declaring required properties has no `model` to read, and reading the context there would invent a value the engine does not have) and QDelegateReqFill (same boundary, from the other side). `partialOk` in reggaefile.d accepts 0 or 3 for those two and nothing else; the differential beside them is what proves the refusal is the RIGHT one, both sides reading empty.
entries.remove_when: required-property injection lands, at which point those documents stop being refusals and the entries must go

entries.reason: MEASURED per binding, not guessed. A non-QObject wrapper only leaks if the binding can ALLOCATE it: QtWidgets has 60 such roots but 14 heap-constructible, Controls 98/15, QML 21/7, Quick 98/16. Two are disposable today — QTreeWidgetItem (its destructor detaches from its owner) and QTextStream (nothing in the binding takes one, so its transfer surface is provably empty). The rest still leak, which is the safe error, and ownership-gate-* refuses to let one be enabled without classifying its surface.
entries.remove_when: every disposable non-QObject the binding constructs has an audited transfer surface

entries.reason: MEASURED: destroy a QTreeWidget that owns a QTreeWidgetItem and the item's D wrapper still reports _cpp non-null — checkAlive() never fires. QLayoutItem/QTreeWidgetItem have no destroyed() signal, so nothing invalidates the wrapper. This also rules out the obvious fix: a finalizer that asks parent()/treeWidget() before deleting is CALLING THROUGH the freed pointer, so the query is itself the use-after-free. Ownership has to be dropped at the call that transfers it, not queried at destruction. The probe ASSERTS the gap: when it fails, the gap is closed and this entry must be removed.
entries.remove_when: transfer-in APIs are declared and the emitter drops D ownership at that call, or the types are not D-constructible at all

entries.reason: A generated ctor is `__cpp_new` then the C++ constructor then _register(). If the C++ constructor throws and the Lippincott layer turns it into a QtCppException, nothing owns the allocated block: the wrapper was never registered and no finalizer knows the pointer.
entries.remove_when: a scope guard frees the block unless construction and registration both complete

entries.reason: A pointer a Qt API returns is now BORROWED by default (holder: _ownedByD), which is the safe direction and fixed the ~QThread deadlock. It is not the whole answer: an API that genuinely transfers ownership out (a factory return, QLayout::takeAt) now leaks instead of crashing, and the binding has no per-method ownership metadata to tell the two apart.
entries.remove_when: every pointer-returning method carries ownership metadata (owned / borrowed / transfer-out) instead of a single conservative default

entries.reason: `property alias inner: box.color` — an alias whose target is a VALUE-TYPE property of a child — is refused with "alias target is unsupported". Found while building the two-locals fixture for the CompilationContext question; the alias had to be dropped for the fixture to compile, which is how it surfaced. Aliases onto a child's scalar and onto base properties work. Left as a gap rather than fixed on measurement, not instinct: the shape appears ZERO times across Qt's five Controls styles, and the value-type channel is where a wrongly-typed field once cost eight link failures here.
entries.remove_when: an alias whose target is a child's value-type property compiles, or is refused with a reason

entries.reason: componentComplete runs in REVERSE creation order and ours runs forward. QQmlObjectCreator::finalize keeps every object it built on a stack and drains it with pop(), so of two siblings the SECOND completes first; we complete each child the moment we create it. It shows on DelayButton (Basic and Fusion): a QQuickText freezes its baselineOffset at its FIRST layout and never recomputes it on a later resize, so which sibling completes first decides which one is laid out at height 0. Probed step by step — dc0 completes with the group still 0 high and reads ascent - height/2 = 5.34375; dc1, appended into a group that already has a height, reads the ascent, 14.84375. The engine is the mirror, and reversing reproduces it exactly. Everything else about the two children agrees, including every property either side assigns. Two earlier readings of this entry (child order, then layout order) were disproved by measurement. REFINED, and this is the part to start from: NEITHER ordering reproduces the engine on its own. Per-LEVEL reverse fixes DelayButton in Basic and Fusion and breaks Universal's by exactly 3 — half of a height — while GLOBAL reverse (drained once at the root, which is literally what QQmlObjectCreator::finalize does) gives 19.34375 to both of Basic's ClippedText siblings where the engine gives 14.84375 and 5.34375. So the difference is not ordering alone: there is a third factor, and it is WHEN THE PARENT APPLIES ITS GEOMETRY relative to the child's first layout. A QQuickControl sizes its contentItem in its own componentComplete, so which of the two happens first decides which layout state the child freezes. Measured over the full matrix the three parts together give 229 where the tree gives 235.
entries.remove_when: the order in which a child's first layout and its parent's geometry happen matches the engine's, measured on DelayButton in all three of Basic, Fusion and Universal at once — reversing completion alone does not do it. The work is on the branch `wip/completion-order`, with the three parts and their measurements in its commit message.

entries.reason: A default child whose type our registry does not know is DROPPED, with its id, and the document counts a skipped member — `Timer` is the plain case, and a Timer is the most ordinary piece of application machinery there is. The refusal is not because the object cannot be built: measured directly, `createQmlObject("QtQuick", "Timer")` and `createQmlObject("QtQml", "Timer")` both return a live QQmlTimer, which is the same containment path the compiler already uses for a type no D subclass can wrap (dcEngineUri). What is missing is the decision: that path is only taken when `uriForType(childType)` and `g_qmlCxxType` both answer, and for a type outside the binding neither does, so the child is dropped instead of being built from the document's own imports. NOT a binding gap for SpinBox reasons: QQmlTimer links fine, it is simply not in spec_cxx_controls.json. The risk that has to be handled first is silence — with no registry entry the child's own members (interval, running, repeat, onTriggered) have to go through the meta channel or be refused one by one, and a Timer that is built but never runs is worse than one honestly skipped. REFINED. It is FOUR of the fifteen demoted application documents, not one: `Timer` (ATimerCounter), `ListModel` (AListModel and AListView) and `RowLayout` (ALayouts) — the largest single cluster left in that corpus. And the risk written here first was overstated: a child that is built but does nothing cannot be silently wrong at the DEFAULT level, because the o3 gate judges behaviour and would demote the document — ATimerCounter's own Text renders the tick count, so a Timer that never fires changes the frame. The real blocker is narrower and it is TYPING THE MEMBERS: the engine-instanced path compiles a child's members from the registry, so with no entry for the type each `interval: 1000000` is refused one by one and the document gains a child that does nothing plus a pile of partials. What is needed alongside the URI decision is an assignment that takes its type from the VALUE rather than from the property, which is a second mechanism and not a line.
entries.remove_when: a default child of a type outside the registry is built by the engine from the document's imports AND its members are assigned by name with the value's own type, with ATimerCounter, AListModel, AListView and ALayouts judged rather than skipped

entries.reason:
A QML id is visible throughout the DOCUMENT, at any depth; ours resolves one level only. Reduced to the two documents that differ by nothing else:
    Item { property int w: kid.width; Rectangle { id: kid; width: 30 } }            compiles
    Item { property int w: kid.width; Row { Rectangle { id: kid; width: 30 } } }    refused
The second reports "the initial binding of property 'w' (int) is not supported". It is three of the fifteen demoted application documents — ALocalType (`a.width + b.width + c.width`, three ATiles in a Row), AControlsApp (`slider.value`, a Slider in a Column) and AInlineComponent (`mid.width`, a Chip in a Row) — and it is invisible in Qt's own styles, which put almost everything one level down. Nesting a child inside a layout is how application QML is written, so this costs more than the count suggests. ALoaderInline looks the same and is NOT this: its `loader` IS a direct child, and what it reads is `loader.item`, an Item-valued property that only exists at run time.
entries.remove_when: an id declared anywhere in the document resolves from anywhere in it, with its accessor chain, and ALocalType, AControlsApp and AInlineComponent are judged rather than skipped
